title: Breaker-points tune-up: points, dwell and timing
warnings: Always set dwell before timing. Changing dwell moves the timing.
Disconnect and plug the vacuum advance hose when setting base timing (unless the spec says otherwise).
steps: Remove the cap and rotor. Inspect the cap for carbon tracking and cracks, and the rotor tip for burning.
Replace points and condenser. Put a small dab of cam lube on the distributor cam.
Bump the engine until the point rubbing block sits on a cam lobe peak. Set the gap with a feeler gauge (see spec for the engine).
Install rotor and cap. Connect the dwell meter (one lead to the coil negative/distributor side, one to ground).
Crank or idle and read dwell. Adjust (GM window distributors: Allen key through the window while running; others: adjust the gap). Smaller gap = more dwell.
Warm the engine to operating temperature. Disconnect and plug the vacuum advance hose.
Hook up the timing light to the #1 plug wire. Loosen the distributor hold-down just enough to turn it.
Set base timing to the underhood label/spec at the specified idle rpm. Tighten the hold-down and recheck.
Reconnect the vacuum advance. Rev the engine and confirm the timing advances smoothly.
Re-adjust idle speed and mixture as needed.
